description: Extensive question bank derived from Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA notes (Chapter 11.7). Covers regional imbalance, rural poverty, unemployment, agricultural dependence, drought, water scarcity, infrastructure gaps, and urban-rural disparity. Verify against latest official sources before formal examination use.

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is regional imbalance?

options.A: Equal distribution of income across all districts
options.B: Unequal distribution of income, investment, employment, infrastructure, education, healthcare and economic opportunities among different regions of a State
options.C: A temporary shortage of rainfall in a region
options.D: The migration of people from one state to another

questions.explanation: Regional imbalance is the unequal distribution of income, investment, employment, infrastructure, education, healthcare and economic opportunities among different regions of a State.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Why is regional imbalance an important issue in Karnataka?

options.A: Because all districts have equal industrial development
options.B: Because economic activity and high-value employment are concentrated in Bengaluru and parts of southern and coastal Karnataka, while several northern, north-eastern and interior districts face weaker industrialisation and lower incomes
options.C: Because Karnataka has no coastal region
options.D: Because agriculture is banned in northern Karnataka

questions.explanation: Economic activity and high-value employment are concentrated in Bengaluru and parts of southern and coastal Karnataka, while several northern, north-eastern and interior districts face comparatively weaker industrialisation, lower incomes, lower urbanisation or gaps in public infrastructure.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which broad regions are commonly discussed in the context of Karnataka's regional disparities?

options.A: Only the coastal belt versus Bengaluru
options.B: The relatively developed southern and coastal belts contrasted with parts of Kalyana Karnataka and other backward interior areas
options.C: Only northern Karnataka versus southern Karnataka
options.D: Only urban versus rural areas

questions.explanation: The relatively developed southern and coastal belts are often contrasted with parts of Kalyana Karnataka and other backward interior areas. This is a broad analytical comparison; conditions vary significantly between districts and taluks.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is Kalyana Karnataka?

options.A: A coastal region of Karnataka
options.B: The officially recognised regional development area comprising Bidar, Kalaburagi, Yadgir, Raichur, Koppal and Ballari districts
options.C: A district in southern Karnataka
options.D: The capital region of Karnataka

questions.explanation: Kalyana Karnataka is the officially recognised regional development area comprising Bidar, Kalaburagi, Yadgir, Raichur, Koppal and Ballari districts. The region has a special constitutional development framework under Article 371J.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is Article 371J?

options.A: A provision for special status to coastal Karnataka
options.B: A constitutional provision providing special provisions for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region (now Kalyana Karnataka), including measures for equitable opportunities in public employment and education and a development board
options.C: An article relating to Panchayati Raj
options.D: An article relating to fundamental duties

questions.explanation: Article 371J of the Constitution provides special provisions for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region, now called Kalyana Karnataka, including measures for equitable opportunities in public employment and education and a development board.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the Kalyana Karnataka Region Development Board (KKRDB)?

options.A: A private company in Bengaluru
options.B: The regional development body established to support targeted development in the Kalyana Karnataka region through projects and allocations in areas such as education, health, infrastructure and livelihoods
options.C: A committee to study rainfall patterns
options.D: A board that issues currency notes

questions.explanation: KKRDB is the regional development body established to support targeted development in the Kalyana Karnataka region through projects and allocations in areas such as education, health, infrastructure and livelihoods.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the purpose of the High-Power Committee for Redressal of Regional Imbalances?

options.A: To conduct elections in Karnataka
options.B: To assess regional backwardness and recommend targeted measures to reduce inter-district and intra-district disparities
options.C: To distribute foodgrains through fair-price shops
options.D: To manage groundwater resources

questions.explanation: The committee chaired by D. M. Nanjundappa assessed regional backwardness and recommended targeted measures to reduce inter-district and intra-district disparities.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the Nanjundappa Committee associated with?

options.A: The 2002 committee report on regional imbalances in Karnataka, which classified taluks according to levels of backwardness and recommended special development measures
options.B: The 1950 committee on fundamental rights
options.C: The 1991 committee on economic reforms
options.D: The 2019 committee on water scarcity

questions.explanation: The 2002 committee report on regional imbalances in Karnataka, chaired by D. M. Nanjundappa, classified taluks according to levels of backwardness and recommended special development measures.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What are the major causes of regional imbalance?

options.A: Only differences in rainfall
options.B: Historical differences in investment, location of industries, uneven irrigation, transport connectivity, urbanisation, education and health facilities, access to markets, natural-resource conditions and public-investment patterns
options.C: Only differences in population size
options.D: Only differences in language spoken

questions.explanation: Historical differences in investment, location of industries, uneven irrigation, transport connectivity, urbanisation, education and health facilities, access to markets, natural-resource conditions and public-investment patterns are major causes.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What are the consequences of regional imbalance?

options.A: Only increased agricultural output
options.B: Migration, concentration of population in major cities, unequal incomes, underemployment, pressure on urban infrastructure, weaker local markets and uneven human-development outcomes
options.C: Only improved infrastructure in all districts
options.D: Only reduced urbanisation

questions.explanation: Consequences include migration, concentration of population in major cities, unequal incomes, underemployment, pressure on urban infrastructure, weaker local markets and uneven human-development outcomes.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What measures can reduce regional imbalance?

options.A: Only building more IT parks in Bengaluru
options.B: District-specific industrial policies, quality roads and rail connectivity, irrigation and drinking-water projects, school and hospital improvements, skill training, decentralised urban growth, local enterprise support and transparent outcome-based regional funding
options.C: Only increasing migration to cities
options.D: Only reducing agricultural production

questions.explanation: Measures include district-specific industrial policies, quality roads and rail connectivity, irrigation and drinking-water projects, school and hospital improvements, skill training, decentralised urban growth, local enterprise support and transparent outcome-based regional funding.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which districts are part of Kalyana Karnataka?

options.A: Bengaluru, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi, Belagavi and Shivamogga
options.B: Bidar, Kalaburagi, Yadgir, Raichur, Koppal and Ballari
options.C: Tumakuru, Chitradurga, Davanagere, Kolar and Chikkaballapur
options.D: Udupi, Dakshina Kannada, Uttara Kannada, Kodagu and Hassan

questions.explanation: Kalyana Karnataka comprises Bidar, Kalaburagi, Yadgir, Raichur, Koppal and Ballari districts.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the difference between Article 371J and KKRDB?

options.A: They are the same thing
options.B: Article 371J is a constitutional provision; KKRDB is a regional development institution
options.C: Article 371J is a development board; KKRDB is a constitutional article
options.D: Both are committees chaired by the Governor

questions.explanation: Article 371J is a constitutional provision; the KKRDB is a regional development institution. They are not the same thing.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7 (Common Examination Traps)

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: When was the Nanjundappa Committee report submitted?
questions.explanation: The Nanjundappa Committee report is associated with 2002; do not confuse it with Article 371J.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7 (Common Examination Traps)

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which article of the Constitution provides special provisions for Kalyana Karnataka?

options.A: Article 370
options.B: Article 371J
options.C: Article 356
options.D: Article 32

questions.explanation: Article 371J provides special provisions for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region, now called Kalyana Karnataka.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is rural poverty?

options.A: A condition in which people living in rural areas lack sufficient income or resources to meet basic needs such as food, housing, healthcare, education, sanitation and secure livelihoods
options.B: A condition in which urban households lack cars
options.C: A situation where all rural people are employed
options.D: A situation where agriculture is not practised

questions.explanation: Rural poverty is a condition in which people living in rural areas lack sufficient income or resources to meet basic needs such as food, housing, healthcare, education, sanitation and secure livelihoods.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What are the main causes of rural poverty in Karnataka?

options.A: Only lack of rainfall
options.B: Small and fragmented landholdings, rain-fed farming, low farm productivity, seasonal employment, indebtedness, low non-farm job availability, price fluctuations, social disadvantage and limited access to quality services
options.C: Only high industrial development
options.D: Only overpopulation in cities

questions.explanation: Main causes include small and fragmented landholdings, rain-fed farming, low farm productivity, seasonal employment, indebtedness, low non-farm job availability, price fluctuations, social disadvantage and limited access to quality services.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Why can agricultural households be vulnerable to poverty?

options.A: Because their income may depend on rainfall, crop yields, input prices and market prices, and a crop failure or price fall can sharply reduce household income
options.B: Because they always receive guaranteed prices
options.C: Because they have no access to any government scheme
options.D: Because they are exempt from all taxes

questions.explanation: Their income may depend on rainfall, crop yields, input prices and market prices. A crop failure or price fall can sharply reduce household income, especially when there is no alternative livelihood.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is multidimensional poverty?

options.A: Poverty measured only by income
options.B: A measure of overlapping deprivations in areas such as health, education and standard of living, rather than considering income alone
options.C: Poverty that affects only urban areas
options.D: Poverty that lasts for only one day

questions.explanation: Multidimensional poverty measures overlapping deprivations in areas such as health, education and standard of living, rather than considering income alone.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: According to NITI Aayog's 2023 discussion paper, what was Karnataka's multidimensional poverty headcount ratio in 2019-21?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog's 2023 discussion paper estimated that Karnataka's multidimensional poverty headcount ratio fell from 12.77% in 2015-16 to 7.58% in 2019-21.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What was Karnataka's multidimensional poverty headcount ratio in 2015-16 according to NITI Aayog's 2023 discussion paper?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog's 2023 discussion paper estimated that Karnataka's multidimensional poverty headcount ratio fell from 12.77% in 2015-16 to 7.58% in 2019-21.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the difference between poverty ratio and poverty gap?

options.A: The poverty ratio measures the proportion of people below a defined poverty line; the poverty gap measures how far, on average, poor people's incomes or consumption fall below that line
options.B: The poverty ratio measures income; the poverty gap measures expenditure
options.C: They are the same thing
options.D: The poverty ratio applies only to urban areas; the poverty gap only to rural areas

questions.explanation: The poverty ratio measures the proportion of people below a defined poverty line. The poverty gap measures how far, on average, poor people's incomes or consumption fall below that line.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How does MGNREGA address rural poverty?

options.A: It provides a legal guarantee of up to 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to each rural household whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work
options.B: It provides free housing to all rural families
options.C: It provides loans at zero interest to farmers
options.D: It provides free education to all children

questions.explanation: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act provides a legal guarantee of up to 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to each rural household whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work, subject to the Act and scheme rules.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How does the Public Distribution System help vulnerable households?

options.A: It distributes eligible foodgrains through fair-price shops under the National Food Security Act and related rules, helping protect food security and reduce the burden of food expenditure
options.B: It provides employment guarantee for 100 days
options.C: It provides free electricity to farmers
options.D: It provides interest-free loans to small industries

questions.explanation: The PDS distributes eligible foodgrains through fair-price shops under the National Food Security Act and related rules, helping protect food security and reduce the burden of food expenditure.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: How can rural poverty be reduced in Karnataka?

options.A: By improving farm productivity, irrigation, rural roads, storage and market access; promoting dairy, fisheries, horticulture and non-farm work; strengthening education and health; expanding skills; and ensuring effective social protection
options.B: By banning agriculture in rural areas
options.C: By forcing all rural people to migrate to cities
options.D: By reducing government spending on rural areas

questions.explanation: Rural poverty can be reduced by improving farm productivity, irrigation, rural roads, storage and market access; promoting dairy, fisheries, horticulture and non-farm work; strengthening education and health; expanding skills; and ensuring effective social protection.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Why should the NITI Aayog 2019-21 multidimensional poverty estimate not be quoted as a 2026 poverty rate?

options.A: Because it is a survey-period estimate, not a 2026 real-time poverty rate
options.B: Because it was conducted by a private agency
options.C: Because it only covers urban areas
options.D: Because it uses income alone

questions.explanation: The NITI Aayog 2019-21 estimate is a survey-period estimate, not a 2026 real-time poverty rate. Do not quote it as a 2026 poverty rate.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7 (Common Examination Traps)

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is unemployment?

options.A: A situation in which a person who is able and willing to work and is seeking work does not obtain employment, as defined by the relevant statistical measure
options.B: A situation where a person works fewer hours than desired
options.C: A situation where more people are engaged in an activity than needed
options.D: A situation where work is available only during particular seasons

questions.explanation: Unemployment is a situation in which a person who is able and willing to work and is seeking work does not obtain employment, as defined by the relevant statistical measure.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the difference between unemployment and underemployment?

options.A: Unemployment means a person is without work but seeking and available for work; underemployment occurs when a person works fewer hours than desired or performs work that does not adequately use their skills or productive capacity
options.B: Unemployment applies only to rural areas; underemployment only to urban areas
options.C: They are the same thing
options.D: Underemployment means a person is not seeking work

questions.explanation: Unemployment means a person is without work but seeking and available for work. Underemployment occurs when a person works fewer hours than desired or performs work that does not adequately use their skills or productive capacity.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is disguised unemployment?

options.A: A situation where a person is without work but seeking work
options.B: A situation where more people are engaged in an activity than are actually needed, so the marginal productivity of some workers may be zero or very low
options.C: A situation where work is available only during particular seasons
options.D: A situation where a person works fewer hours than desired

questions.explanation: Disguised unemployment occurs when more people are engaged in an activity than are actually needed, so the marginal productivity of some workers may be zero or very low. It is often discussed in relation to family-based agriculture.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is seasonal unemployment?

options.A: Unemployment that occurs when work is available only during particular seasons, such as sowing and harvesting periods in agriculture or seasonal tourism
options.B: Unemployment that affects only educated youth
options.C: Unemployment caused by automation
options.D: Unemployment that lasts for many years

questions.explanation: Seasonal unemployment occurs when work is available only during particular seasons, such as sowing and harvesting periods in agriculture or seasonal tourism.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What are the major causes of unemployment in Karnataka?

options.A: Only lack of rainfall
options.B: Skill mismatch, uneven industrial location, insufficient labour-intensive job creation, automation, seasonal agricultural work, slow growth of some local economies and competition for formal-sector jobs
options.C: Only overpopulation
options.D: Only government policies

questions.explanation: Major causes include skill mismatch, uneven industrial location, insufficient labour-intensive job creation, automation, seasonal agricultural work, slow growth of some local economies and competition for formal-sector jobs.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Why can educated unemployment occur even in a growing economy?

options.A: Because the qualifications and skills of job seekers may not match vacancies; employers may require experience or specialised skills; and the number of applicants may exceed available formal jobs
options.B: Because educated people do not want to work
options.C: Because there are no jobs in the economy
options.D: Because education is not valued

questions.explanation: The qualifications and skills of job seekers may not match vacancies; employers may require experience or specialised skills; and the number of applicants may exceed available formal jobs.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)?

options.A: The official large-scale labour-force survey conducted by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, providing estimates of labour-force participation, worker-population ratio and unemployment
options.B: A survey conducted by the Reserve Bank of India
options.C: A survey conducted by NITI Aayog
options.D: A survey conducted by the Election Commission

questions.explanation: PLFS is the official large-scale labour-force survey conducted by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation. It provides estimates of labour-force participation, worker-population ratio and unemployment.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What does the unemployment rate measure?

options.A: The percentage of unemployed persons in the total population
options.B: The percentage of unemployed persons in the labour force, not the percentage of the entire population
options.C: The percentage of employed persons in the total population
options.D: The percentage of people below the poverty line

questions.explanation: The unemployment rate is the percentage of unemployed persons in the labour force, not the percentage of the entire population.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the labour force?

options.A: All persons in the total population
options.B: Employed persons plus unemployed persons who are seeking and/or available for work under the survey's definitions
options.C: Only employed persons
options.D: Only unemployed persons

questions.explanation: The labour force consists of employed persons plus unemployed persons who are seeking and/or available for work under the survey's definitions.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the difference between usual status and current weekly status in PLFS?

options.A: Usual status classifies activity over a longer reference period, generally 365 days; current weekly status uses the seven days preceding the survey
options.B: Usual status uses 7 days; current weekly status uses 365 days
options.C: Both use the same reference period
options.D: Usual status applies only to urban areas; current weekly status only to rural areas

questions.explanation: Usual status classifies activity over a longer reference period, generally 365 days; current weekly status uses the seven days preceding the survey. The two measures can produce different unemployment estimates.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the reference period for usual status in PLFS?

options.A: 7 days
options.B: 30 days
options.C: 365 days
options.D: 100 days

questions.explanation: Usual status classifies activity over a longer reference period, generally 365 days.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the reference period for current weekly status in PLFS?

options.A: 7 days preceding the survey
options.B: 30 days preceding the survey
options.C: 365 days preceding the survey
options.D: 100 days preceding the survey

questions.explanation: Current weekly status uses the seven days preceding the survey.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What measures can improve employment in Karnataka?

options.A: Industry-linked skilling, apprenticeships, labour-intensive manufacturing, MSME growth, rural non-farm employment, tourism, construction, care services, start-up support and better job-matching systems
options.B: Banning all private companies
options.C: Reducing the number of schools
options.D: Stopping all migration to cities

questions.explanation: Measures include industry-linked skilling, apprenticeships, labour-intensive manufacturing, MSME growth, rural non-farm employment, tourism, construction, care services, start-up support and better job-matching systems.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the denominator of the unemployment rate?

options.A: Total population
options.B: Labour force
options.C: Number of employed persons
options.D: Number of persons below poverty line

questions.explanation: Unemployment rate is calculated with reference to the labour force, not the total population.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7 (Common Examination Traps)

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: MGNREGA guarantees up to how many days of wage employment?

options.A: 100 days per rural household per financial year
options.B: 100 days to each individual member of a rural household
options.C: 365 days per rural household per financial year
options.D: 50 days per urban household per financial year

questions.explanation: MGNREGA guarantees up to 100 days of wage employment per rural household, not 100 days to each individual member.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7 (Common Examination Traps)

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is agricultural dependence?

options.A: A high reliance of households, employment or local economic activity on farming and allied activities for income and livelihoods
options.B: The share of agriculture in GSDP only
options.C: The number of tractors in a district
options.D: The area under a single crop

questions.explanation: Agricultural dependence refers to a high reliance of households, employment or local economic activity on farming and allied activities for income and livelihoods.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Why is dependence on agriculture a weakness when it is excessive?

options.A: Because agriculture is exposed to rainfall, drought, pests, input costs and volatile market prices, and heavy dependence on one climate-sensitive livelihood can make household income unstable
options.B: Because agriculture never produces any output
options.C: Because agriculture is illegal in Karnataka
options.D: Because farmers do not pay taxes

questions.explanation: Agriculture is exposed to rainfall, drought, pests, input costs and volatile market prices. Heavy dependence on one climate-sensitive livelihood can make household income unstable.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Does agriculture contribute the largest share of Karnataka's GSDP?

options.A: Yes, agriculture is the largest sector
options.B: No, in the 2025-26 advance estimates the primary sector accounted for about 11.43% of current-price GSVA, while services accounted for about 69.87%
options.C: Yes, agriculture accounts for about 69.87% of GSVA
options.D: No, agriculture accounts for about 50% of GSVA

questions.explanation: In the 2025-26 advance estimates, the primary sector accounted for about 11.43% of current-price GSVA, while services accounted for about 69.87%. Agriculture remains important for livelihoods even though its output share is much smaller than the services sector's.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What was the primary sector's share of current-price GSVA in Karnataka as per 2025-26 advance estimates?

options.A: About 11.43%
options.B: About 69.87%
options.C: About 25.00%
options.D: About 50.00%

questions.explanation: In the 2025-26 advance estimates, the primary sector accounted for about 11.43% of current-price GSVA.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What was the services sector's share of current-price GSVA in Karnataka as per 2025-26 advance estimates?

options.A: About 11.43%
options.B: About 69.87%
options.C: About 25.00%
options.D: About 50.00%

questions.explanation: In the 2025-26 advance estimates, services accounted for about 69.87% of current-price GSVA.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Why is the employment share of agriculture important?

options.A: Because agriculture can employ a larger share of workers than its share of output, indicating lower average labour productivity and the need for productive non-farm employment and higher-value agricultural activities
options.B: Because it shows agriculture is the largest sector in GSDP
options.C: Because it shows farmers are the richest group
options.D: Because it shows agriculture is declining in employment

questions.explanation: Agriculture can employ a larger share of workers than its share of output, indicating lower average labour productivity and the need for productive non-farm employment and higher-value agricultural activities.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is low agricultural productivity?

options.A: Output per unit of land, labour or other input is relatively low
options.B: Output per unit of land is very high
options.C: The number of crops grown is very high
options.D: The number of farmers is very low

questions.explanation: Low agricultural productivity means output per unit of land, labour or other input is relatively low. Causes can include small holdings, limited irrigation, inadequate mechanisation, weak extension services, poor soil health and post-harvest losses.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What are the causes of low agricultural productivity?

options.A: Small holdings, limited irrigation, inadequate mechanisation, weak extension services, poor soil health and post-harvest losses
options.B: Excessive rainfall and flooding
options.C: Too many tractors and machines
options.D: Too much use of fertilisers

questions.explanation: Causes of low agricultural productivity can include small holdings, limited irrigation, inadequate mechanisation, weak extension services, poor soil health and post-harvest losses.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is crop diversification?

options.A: The shift from dependence on a narrow range of crops towards a wider mix of food crops, pulses, oilseeds, horticulture, plantation crops and allied activities based on agro-climatic suitability
options.B: The practice of growing only one crop
options.C: The process of destroying all crops
options.D: The process of importing all food

questions.explanation: Crop diversification is the shift from dependence on a narrow range of crops towards a wider mix of food crops, pulses, oilseeds, horticulture, plantation crops and allied activities based on agro-climatic suitability.

options.D: By reducing all rural infrastructure

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy

options.A: Processing, grading, storage, packaging, branding and direct market access can increase the share of the final consumer value received by producers and reduce post-harvest losses

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is drought?

options.A: A prolonged period of abnormally low water availability caused by deficient rainfall, high evaporative demand or inadequate surface and groundwater resources relative to needs
options.B: A short period of heavy rainfall
options.C: A situation where water demand equals supply
options.D: A situation where rivers overflow

questions.explanation: Drought is a prolonged period of abnormally low water availability caused by deficient rainfall, high evaporative demand or inadequate surface and groundwater resources relative to needs.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is meteorological drought?

options.A: A rainfall deficiency compared with the long-term normal for a specified period and area
options.B: A shortage of soil moisture affecting crops
options.C: A shortage of water in rivers and reservoirs
options.D: A shortage of drinking water in cities

questions.explanation: Meteorological drought is a rainfall deficiency compared with the long-term normal for a specified period and area.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is agricultural drought?

options.A: A rainfall deficiency compared with the long-term normal
options.B: A shortage of soil moisture to meet crop water requirements, adversely affecting crop growth and yields
options.C: A shortage of water in rivers, reservoirs and groundwater
options.D: A shortage of water for industrial use

questions.explanation: Agricultural drought occurs when soil moisture is insufficient to meet crop water requirements, adversely affecting crop growth and yields.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is hydrological drought?

options.A: A rainfall deficiency compared with the long-term normal
options.B: A shortage of soil moisture affecting crops
options.C: A shortage of water in rivers, reservoirs, lakes and groundwater systems
options.D: A shortage of water in urban households

questions.explanation: Hydrological drought is a shortage of water in rivers, reservoirs, lakes and groundwater systems.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Why is Karnataka vulnerable to drought?

options.A: Large parts of the State lie in rain-shadow or semi-arid regions, rainfall is unevenly distributed, and many agricultural areas depend heavily on the South-West and North-East monsoons
options.B: Because the entire state receives very heavy rainfall
options.C: Because the state has no agriculture
options.D: Because the state has no rivers

questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which broad parts of Karnataka are especially drought-prone?

options.A: Only the coastal districts
options.B: Several interior districts of north, central and south-eastern Karnataka
options.C: Only Bengaluru Urban
options.D: Only the Western Ghats

questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What are the effects of drought on the economy?

options.A: Crop losses, livestock stress, reduced rural wages, distress migration, higher drinking-water costs, groundwater depletion, lower reservoir storage and increased public expenditure on relief
options.B: Increased crop yields and higher rural wages
options.C: Reduced public expenditure on relief
options.D: Increased groundwater levels

questions.explanation: Effects of drought include crop losses, livestock stress, reduced rural wages, distress migration, higher drinking-water costs, groundwater depletion, lower reservoir storage and increased public expenditure on relief.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is drought-proofing?

options.A: Reducing vulnerability through watershed development, rainwater harvesting, soil-moisture conservation, tank restoration, efficient irrigation, drought-resilient crops and diversified livelihoods
options.B: Building more houses in drought-prone areas
options.C: Increasing water-intensive crops in drought-prone areas
options.D: Banning all agriculture in drought-prone areas

questions.explanation: Drought-proofing means reducing vulnerability through watershed development, rainwater harvesting, soil-moisture conservation, tank restoration, efficient irrigation, drought-resilient crops and diversified livelihoods.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the role of watershed development?

options.A: It manages land and water within a drainage area through contour bunding, check dams, farm ponds, vegetative measures and groundwater recharge
options.B: It builds large dams on major rivers
options.C: It constructs highways across watersheds
options.D: It shifts all agriculture to urban areas

questions.explanation: Watershed development manages land and water within a drainage area through contour bunding, check dams, farm ponds, vegetative measures and groundwater recharge.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is micro-irrigation?

options.B: It floods the entire field with water
options.C: It uses only rainwater for irrigation
options.D: It uses seawater for irrigation

questions.explanation: Micro-irrigation delivers water near the plant root zone through systems such as drip and sprinkler irrigation, reducing conveyance and application losses when properly designed and maintained.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Why should drought be treated as a recurring structural risk rather than only a disaster-relief issue?

options.A: Because climatic variability and water stress repeatedly affect livelihoods, and long-term resilience requires changes in land use, cropping patterns, water management and rural economic diversification
options.B: Because droughts never recur
options.C: Because disaster relief is always sufficient
options.D: Because agriculture does not depend on water

questions.explanation: Because climatic variability and water stress repeatedly affect livelihoods. Long-term resilience requires changes in land use, cropping patterns, water management and rural economic diversification.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is the difference between drought and water scarcity?

options.A: They are exactly the same concept
options.B: Drought is a climatic or hydrological event involving deficient water availability over time; water scarcity can be chronic and may result from high demand, poor management, pollution, unequal access or limited infrastructure even without drought

options.D: Water scarcity is always caused by drought

questions.explanation: Drought is a climatic or hydrological event involving deficient water availability over time. Water scarcity can be chronic and may result from high demand, poor management, pollution, unequal access or limited infrastructure even without drought.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Why are drought declarations in Karnataka considered season- and taluk-specific?

options.A: Because exact drought declarations must be checked against the relevant Government notification and may change by season and taluk

questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is water scarcity?

options.A: A situation when available usable water is insufficient in quantity or quality to meet domestic, agricultural, industrial and ecological needs
options.B: A situation when water is abundant
options.C: A situation when rainfall is above normal
options.D: A situation when rivers are overflowing

questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Why does Karnataka face inter-regional water stress?

options.A: Rainfall and river flows are unevenly distributed, many interior areas are semi-arid, demand is rising in cities and agriculture, and river basins are shared with neighbouring States

options.C: Because Karnataka has no rivers

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: What is groundwater over-exploitation?

options.A: Withdrawal of groundwater at a rate that cannot be sustainably replenished, leading to falling water tables, higher pumping costs and possible deterioration of water quality

options.C: Using surface water for irrigation

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy

options.D: Skill training

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cause of rural poverty in Karnataka?

options.D: Indebtedness

questions.explanation: Causes of rural poverty include small and fragmented landholdings, rain-fed farming, low farm productivity, seasonal employment, indebtedness, low non-farm job availability, price fluctuations, social disadvantage and limited access to quality services. questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a measure to reduce rural poverty in Karnataka?

options.A: Improving farm productivity
options.B: Promoting dairy, fisheries, horticulture and non-farm work
options.C: Reducing access to education and health
options.D: Ensuring effective social protection

questions.explanation: Rural poverty can be reduced by improving farm productivity, irrigation, rural roads, storage and market access; promoting dairy, fisheries, horticulture and non-farm work; strengthening education and health; expanding skills; and ensuring effective social protection. questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy

options.D: Automation

questions.explanation: Major causes of unemployment include skill mismatch, uneven industrial location, insufficient labour-intensive job creation, automation, seasonal agricultural work, slow growth of some local economies and competition for formal-sector jobs. questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy

options.D: Better job-matching systems

questions.explanation: Measures to improve employment include industry-linked skilling, apprenticeships, labour-intensive manufacturing, MSME growth, rural non-farm employment, tourism, construction, care services, start-up support and better job-matching systems. questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

options.D: Skill-based non-farm employment

questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a drought-proofing measure?

options.A: Watershed development
options.B: Rainwater harvesting
options.C: Promoting water-intensive crops in drought-prone areas
options.D: Drought-resilient crops

questions.explanation: Drought-proofing means reducing vulnerability through watershed development, rainwater harvesting, soil-moisture conservation, tank restoration, efficient irrigation, drought-resilient crops and diversified livelihoods. questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a measure to improve water security in Karnataka?

options.A: Protecting catchments
options.B: Restoring tanks and lakes
options.C: Increasing groundwater extraction without regulation
options.D: Treating and reusing wastewater

questions.explanation: Measures to improve water security include protecting catchments, restoring tanks and lakes, improving irrigation efficiency, treating and reusing wastewater, regulating extraction in stressed areas, recharging aquifers, reducing leakage and promoting crops suited to local water availability. questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

options.D: Broadband expansion

questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

options.D: Improving rural roads and broadband

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about drought in Karnataka is correct?

options.A: Large parts of the State lie in rain-shadow or semi-arid regions, rainfall is unevenly distributed, and many agricultural areas depend heavily on the South-West and North-East monsoons
options.B: The entire State receives uniform heavy rainfall
options.C: Karnataka has no semi-arid regions
options.D: Karnataka does not depend on monsoons

questions.explanation: Large parts of the State lie in rain-shadow or semi-arid regions, rainfall is unevenly distributed, and many agricultural areas depend heavily on the South-West and North-East monsoons.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about water scarcity in Karnataka is correct?

options.A: Rainfall and river flows are unevenly distributed, many interior areas are semi-arid, demand is rising in cities and agriculture, and river basins are shared with neighbouring States
options.B: All regions of Karnataka receive equal rainfall
options.C: Karnataka has no shared river basins
options.D: Water demand is falling in cities and agriculture

questions.explanation: Rainfall and river flows are unevenly distributed, many interior areas are semi-arid, demand is rising in cities and agriculture, and river basins are shared with neighbouring States.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Bengaluru's urban infrastructure is correct?

options.A: Traffic congestion, road capacity, public transport integration, drainage and flooding, water supply, sewage treatment, solid-waste management and affordable housing are persistent challenges
options.B: Bengaluru has no traffic congestion
options.C: Bengaluru has no water supply challenges
options.D: Bengaluru has no solid-waste management issues

questions.explanation: Traffic congestion, road capacity, public transport integration, drainage and flooding, water supply, sewage treatment, solid-waste management and affordable housing are persistent challenges in Bengaluru.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about migration and urban-rural relations is correct?

options.A: Migration can provide income through remittances and improve household opportunities, but rapid migration may also create pressure on urban housing, transport, water, sanitation and public services
options.B: Migration only has negative effects
options.C: Migration only has positive effects
options.D: Migration does not affect urban areas

questions.explanation: Migration can provide income through remittances and improve household opportunities, but rapid migration may also create pressure on urban housing, transport, water, sanitation and public services.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Nanjundappa Committee is correct?

options.A: It was a 2002 committee report on regional imbalances in Karnataka, which classified taluks according to levels of backwardness and recommended special development measures
options.B: It was a 1950 committee on fundamental rights
options.C: It was a 1991 committee on economic reforms
options.D: It was a 2019 committee on water scarcity

questions.explanation: The 2002 committee report on regional imbalances in Karnataka, chaired by D. M. Nanjundappa, classified taluks according to levels of backwardness and recommended special development measures.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Kalyana Karnataka Region Development Board (KKRDB) is correct?

options.A: It is the regional development body established to support targeted development in the Kalyana Karnataka region through projects and allocations in areas such as education, health, infrastructure and livelihoods
options.B: It is a constitutional article
options.C: It is a committee that issues currency notes
options.D: It is a private company in Bengaluru

questions.explanation: KKRDB is the regional development body established to support targeted development in the Kalyana Karnataka region through projects and allocations in areas such as education, health, infrastructure and livelihoods.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about MGNREGA is correct?

options.A: It provides a legal guarantee of up to 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to each rural household whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work, subject to the Act and scheme rules
options.B: It provides 100 days of employment to each individual member of a rural household
options.C: It provides 365 days of employment to each rural household
options.D: It provides employment only to urban households

questions.explanation: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act provides a legal guarantee of up to 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to each rural household whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work, subject to the Act and scheme rules.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Public Distribution System is correct?

options.A: It distributes eligible foodgrains through fair-price shops under the National Food Security Act and related rules, helping protect food security and reduce the burden of food expenditure
options.B: It provides 100 days of employment to rural households
options.C: It provides free electricity to farmers
options.D: It provides interest-free loans to small industries

questions.explanation: The PDS distributes eligible foodgrains through fair-price shops under the National Food Security Act and related rules, helping protect food security and reduce the burden of food expenditure.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about educated unemployment is correct?

options.A: Educated unemployment can occur even in a growing economy because the qualifications and skills of job seekers may not match vacancies; employers may require experience or specialised skills; and the number of applicants may exceed available formal jobs
options.B: Educated unemployment cannot occur in a growing economy
options.C: Educated unemployment is caused only by a lack of education
options.D: Educated unemployment is caused only by government policy

questions.explanation: The qualifications and skills of job seekers may not match vacancies; employers may require experience or specialised skills; and the number of applicants may exceed available formal jobs.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about crop diversification is correct?

options.A: Crop diversification is the shift from dependence on a narrow range of crops towards a wider mix of food crops, pulses, oilseeds, horticulture, plantation crops and allied activities based on agro-climatic suitability
options.B: Crop diversification means growing only one crop
options.C: Crop diversification means destroying all crops
options.D: Crop diversification means importing all food

questions.explanation: Crop diversification is the shift from dependence on a narrow range of crops towards a wider mix of food crops, pulses, oilseeds, horticulture, plantation crops and allied activities based on agro-climatic suitability.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about value addition for farmers is correct?

options.A: Processing, grading, storage, packaging, branding and direct market access can increase the share of the final consumer value received by producers and reduce post-harvest losses
options.B: Value addition means increasing the quantity of raw produce sold
options.C: Value addition means reducing the price of final products
options.D: Value addition means exporting all raw materials

questions.explanation: Processing, grading, storage, packaging, branding and direct market access can increase the share of the final consumer value received by producers and reduce post-harvest losses.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about watershed development is correct?

options.A: Watershed development manages land and water within a drainage area through contour bunding, check dams, farm ponds, vegetative measures and groundwater recharge
options.B: Watershed development builds large dams on major rivers
options.C: Watershed development constructs highways across watersheds
options.D: Watershed development shifts all agriculture to urban areas

questions.explanation: Watershed development manages land and water within a drainage area through contour bunding, check dams, farm ponds, vegetative measures and groundwater recharge.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about micro-irrigation is correct?

options.A: Micro-irrigation delivers water near the plant root zone through systems such as drip and sprinkler irrigation, reducing conveyance and application losses when properly designed and maintained
options.B: Micro-irrigation floods the entire field with water
options.C: Micro-irrigation uses only rainwater for irrigation
options.D: Micro-irrigation uses seawater for irrigation

questions.explanation: Micro-irrigation delivers water near the plant root zone through systems such as drip and sprinkler irrigation, reducing conveyance and application losses when properly designed and maintained.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about groundwater over-exploitation is correct?

options.A: It is withdrawal of groundwater at a rate that cannot be sustainably replenished, leading to falling water tables, higher pumping costs and possible deterioration of water quality
options.B: It is recharging groundwater through rainwater harvesting
options.C: It is using surface water for irrigation
options.D: It is building check dams in watersheds

questions.explanation: Groundwater over-exploitation is withdrawal of groundwater at a rate that cannot be sustainably replenished, leading to falling water tables, higher pumping costs and possible deterioration of water quality.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Jal Jeevan Mission is correct?

options.A: It is a Government of India programme intended to provide functional household tap connections to rural households, with an emphasis on adequate quantity, prescribed quality and regular supply
options.B: It is a programme to build large dams
options.C: It is a programme to provide free electricity to farmers
options.D: It is a programme to promote groundwater over-exploitation

questions.explanation: Jal Jeevan Mission is a Government of India programme intended to provide functional household tap connections to rural households, with an emphasis on adequate quantity, prescribed quality and regular supply.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Atal Bhujal Yojana is correct?

options.A: It is a central groundwater-management scheme that promotes community participation and sustainable groundwater use in selected water-stressed areas
options.B: It is a programme to provide tap connections to rural households
options.C: It is a programme to build highways
options.D: It is a programme to promote water-intensive crops

questions.explanation: Atal Bhujal Yojana is a central groundwater-management scheme that promotes community participation and sustainable groundwater use in selected water-stressed areas. Its coverage and implementation must be checked against official programme records.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the digital divide is correct?

options.A: The digital divide is unequal access to reliable internet, devices, digital literacy and online services between people or regions
options.B: The digital divide is equal access to internet across all regions
options.C: The digital divide is a gap between urban and rural roads
options.D: The digital divide is a gap in electricity supply only

questions.explanation: The digital divide is unequal access to reliable internet, devices, digital literacy and online services between people or regions.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about logistics infrastructure is correct?

options.A: Warehouses, cold chains, freight terminals, ports, roads and railways reduce delays and spoilage, improve supply-chain reliability and make firms more competitive
options.B: Logistics infrastructure increases delays and spoilage
options.C: Logistics infrastructure reduces supply-chain reliability
options.D: Logistics infrastructure makes firms less competitive

questions.explanation: Warehouses, cold chains, freight terminals, ports, roads and railways reduce delays and spoilage, improve supply-chain reliability and make firms more competitive.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following statements about decentralised planning is correct?

options.A: Local institutions can identify area-specific needs and prioritise investments, but they require adequate funds, trained staff, data, accountability and meaningful public participation
options.B: Local institutions do not need funds
options.C: Central planning is always better than decentralised planning
options.D: Public participation is unnecessary in decentralised planning

questions.explanation: Local institutions can identify area-specific needs and prioritise investments, but they require adequate funds, trained staff, data, accountability and meaningful public participation.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a concept with its meaning?

options.A: Regional imbalance — Unequal development between regions within a State
options.B: Regional imbalance — Unequal opportunities and services between urban and rural areas
options.C: Urban-rural disparity — Unequal development between regions within a State
options.D: Poverty ratio — Overlapping deprivations in health, education and living standards

questions.explanation: Regional imbalance = unequal development between regions within a State. Urban-rural disparity = unequal opportunities and services between urban and rural areas. Poverty ratio = share of population below a specified poverty threshold. Multidimensional poverty = overlapping deprivations in health, education and living standards.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7 (Important Comparisons and Concepts)

questions.subject: Karnataka Economy
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a concept with its meaning?

options.A: Urban-rural disparity — Unequal opportunities and services between urban and rural areas
options.B: Urban-rural disparity — Unequal development between regions within a State
options.C: Multidimensional poverty — Share of population below a specified poverty threshold
options.D: Poverty ratio — Overlapping deprivations in health, education and living standards

questions.explanation: Urban-rural disparity = unequal opportunities and services between urban and rural areas. Regional imbalance = unequal development between regions within a State. Multidimensional poverty = overlapping deprivations in health, education and living standards. Poverty ratio = share of population below a specified poverty threshold.
questions.source: Karnataka Economic Weaknesses FDA/SDA Notes, Chapter 11.7 (Important Comparisons and Concepts)
